# Kspec Automation Session - Task Work

**Session ID:** `01KJKCGRAVN1BTZ611MX7EK5H3`
**Iteration:** 1 of 30
**Mode:** Automated (no human in the loop)


### Current State

> **Truncated** (104281 bytes). Fetch full data:
> ```
> kspec session start --json
> ```
>
> Summary: `{}`

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
$kspec-task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

```sh
OK Started task: 01KJK9DV

--- Spec Context ---
Implementing: Ralph Subagent Spawning

Ralph can spawn ACP subagents for dedicated tasks (e.g., PR review). Subagents are separate Claude Code processes with focused prompts. Subagents run sequentially (ralph waits for completion).

Acceptance Criteria (13):
  [ac-1]
    Given: ralph needs subagent
    When: spawn initiated
    Then: new ACP process started with dedicated prompt
  [ac-2]
    Given: subagent spawned
    When: prompt provided
    Then: prompt includes task ref, skill to invoke (/pr-review @task), context, and explicit review-only role boundary (never fix code)
  [ac-3]
    Given: subagent running
    When: ralph behavior
    Then: ralph waits for subagent completion before continuing
  [ac-4]
    Given: subagent runs
    When: display
    Then: subagent output rendered same as main agent (single stream)
  [ac-5]
    Given: subagent completes
    When: signaling
    Then: task status change (completed/needs_review) indicates outcome
  [ac-6]
    Given: multiple pending_review tasks
    When: spawning
    Then: processes one at a time sequentially
  [ac-7]
    Given: subagent runs
    When: resource management
    Then: respects ralph's --max-retries and failure limits
  [ac-8]
    Given: ralph iteration begins
    When: ralph checks task statuses
    Then: pending_review tasks detected trigger subagent spawn by ralph (host) before main agent iteration continues
  [ac-9]
    Given: subagent is running
    When: subagent exceeds timeout (default 10 minutes)
    Then: ralph terminates subagent and marks task automation: needs_review with timeout note
  [ac-10]
    Given: subagent prompt is built
    When: context is assembled
    Then: includes compact identity summaries of task details and linked spec (with CLI fetch commands for full data), and current git branch
  [ac-11]
    Given: subagent output is displayed
    When: rendering to terminal
    Then: output includes [REVIEW SUBAGENT] prefix to distinguish from main agent
  [ac-12]
    Given: subagent successfully merges PR
    When: workflow completes
    Then: subagent must complete the task (kspec task complete) before exiting; ralph verifies task is completed after subagent success
  [ac-13]
    Given: subagent completes review with blocking findings
    When: subagent exits
    Then: task transitions to needs_work; worker picks it up in next iteration as fix cycle

Remember: Add test coverage for each AC and mark tests with // AC: @spec-ref ac-N
```

  01KFH76C (1/21/2026 by @claude) [design, spec-model, meta]
    Cross-feature requirement pattern: How to express that core features (search, validate, export) must support all entity types. When new entity type added, should automatically imply tasks for core features. Options: (1) applies_to field on feature specs, (2) trait on entity types like @trait-searchable, (3) validation warning for missing coverage, (4) parent spec that entity types must satisfy. Surfaced when realizing search doesn't cover inbox.

  01KFHJNZ (1/21/2026 by @claude) [dx, tooling, reflection]
    Reverse spec lookup - kspec which <file> or kspec which <file:line> to find specs/ACs that reference or are implemented by a given code path. Useful for bug fixes to quickly discover what specs need updating. Could scan for // AC: annotations and spec_ref links. Instructive, helps find already-instrumented code.

  01KFPDCY (1/23/2026 by @claude) [ci, testing, dx]
    Add cross-platform CI matrix testing - run core functionality tests on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Would catch issues like Unix-specific commands (which, cp -r) before they reach PR review. Consider: matrix strategy in GitHub Actions, platform-specific test skips where needed, focus on CLI commands and daemon lifecycle.

  01KFQ517 (1/23/2026 by @claude) [e2e, testing, reflection]
    E2E tests: Use isolated port range (not 3456) + cross-platform cleanup. Current approach conflicts with existing daemons. Should use high ephemeral port range and improve cleanup mechanism.

  01KFYAHF (1/26/2026 by @claude) [e2e, dx]
    E2E test dev mode - configure Playwright to work with vite dev server instead of requiring full build for faster test iteration (12+ seconds to 1-2 seconds)

  01KGG6GY (3 weeks ago by @claude)
    Improve derive granularity: Research suggests specs with 4+ ACs are candidates for splitting. Potential enhancements: (1) --by-ac flag to create tasks per AC group, (2) --max-acs N to auto-group, (3) implementation_phases field in specs, (4) derive templates for common patterns (cli-command, api-endpoint), (5) complexity warnings when specs are too large. See session research on task decomposition patterns from Linear, Atlassian, BDD/Example Mapping, and AI coding assistants.

  01KGGEMM (3 weeks ago by @claude) [daemon, dx, deferred]
    Daemon debugging improvements: (1) Add --log-file or --verbose to 'kspec serve start', (2) Log resolved web UI path on startup, (3) Capture and show stderr when daemon fails to start within timeout. Consolidated from @01KFQ586, @01KFQ595, @01KFPH3D.

  01KGGF4Y (3 weeks ago by @claude) [feature, config, dx, deferred]
    Project config file (kspec.config.yaml or .kspecrc): Configure shadow remote URL (enable separate repo for specs), feature toggles, default values (author, priority), validation strictness. Enables multi-repo projects sharing specs and tailoring kspec to project needs. Consolidated from @01KFGVVJ, @01KFGVVN.

  01KGGFB2 (3 weeks ago by @claude) [cli, testing, dx]
    AC test coverage analysis: 'kspec coverage @spec-ref' command to scan codebase for '// AC: @spec ac-N' annotations and report which ACs have test coverage vs gaps. Soft check for review, not blocking. Consolidated from @01KFHJNR, @01KFP9A6.

  01KGGG0K (3 weeks ago by @claude) [shadow, dx, cli]
    Shadow sync improvements: (1) Auto-resolve using rebase/merge-driver for cleaner sync, (2) Make sync warnings visible in CLI output (currently silent unless KSPEC_DEBUG=1), (3) Auto-detect common issues with suggested fixes. Consolidated from @01KFTDA7, @01KFHZR4.

  01KGGKNX (3 weeks ago by @claude) [cli, design, dx]
    CLI array field flag patterns: (1) Generic --clear <field> or --<field> [] for clearing arrays, (2) --add-<field> vs multiple flags for append semantics. Design unified approach for depends-on, tags, blocked-by, etc. Consolidated from @01KFGRV6, @01KFR0KN.

  01KGGP9F (3 weeks ago by @claude) [cli, inbox, dx]
    Inbox CLI improvements: (1) Add filtering to list: --before/--after <date>, --author <name> (--tag exists), (2) Add merge command: 'kspec inbox merge @source @target' for consolidating duplicates, (3) Add --priority and --automation flags to promote command. Consolidated from @01KG95JP, @01KG95JQ, @01KG95JS.

  01KGGPJ6 (3 weeks ago by @claude) [workflow, cli, dx]
    Workflow CLI improvements: (1) 'workflow show' should infer active run like 'workflow next', (2) Warn when --input flags passed but step has no inputs defined, (3) Improve 'workflow show' output format with vertical display, status indicators, indented notes. Consolidated from @01KFKSF6, @01KFKSGC, @01KFKTNR.

  01KGGPSR (3 weeks ago by @claude) [cli, validation, ux]
    Spec item slug/addressing improvements: (1) Warn/error on slug collision when creating items, (2) Make nested requirements addressable by slug (currently kspec item ac add @slug fails for items under requirements:). Consolidated from @01KGDCRG, @01KGDCRJ.

  01KGGTT3 (3 weeks ago by @claude) [cli, batch, dx]
    Expand @trait-multi-ref-batch to remaining commands: trait add/remove, task set --automation, inbox delete, task note. Enables batch operations like 'kspec task note @ref1 @ref2 @ref3 "shared content"'. Consolidated from @01KG71J2, @01KG95JM, @01KFVXBM.

  01KGKVK9 (3 weeks ago by @claude) [cli, reflection]
    Add --spec-ref filter to kspec task list command to filter tasks by linked spec item

  01KGQY6Q (3 weeks ago by @claude) [workflow, cli, dx, deferred]
    Workflow lifecycle CLI design (from mining run 01KFS6MJ): kspec workflow complete @run-ref (mark run completed, archive), kspec workflow cancel @run-ref (cancel abandoned run), kspec workflow cleanup --older-than Nd (auto-cancel stale runs). Extends existing @01KFPH39 auto-cleanup with concrete subcommand design.

  01KGVK8R (3 weeks ago by @claude) [cli, dx, reflection]
    Item list --module flag and tree view: kspec item list --module cli to scope output to a specific module. kspec item tree @module for hierarchical view (features -> requirements). Currently 50+ items display flat, making it hard to find the right parent for new specs. Friction: during automation triage had to grep YAML files to find parent specs.

  01KGWG99 (3 weeks ago by @claude) [reflection, sessions, schema]
    Define typed event data schemas per EventType — session.start, session.update (with tool_call/sessionUpdate variants), session.end, prompt.sent, tool.call, tool.result, note. Current z.unknown() data field makes it impossible to reliably query events without reverse-engineering from real JSONL files.

  01KGWQ2T (3 weeks ago by @claude) [deferred]

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
$kspec-task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

      "content": "Implementation notes:\n\n## Fix 1: O(1) seq assignment in appendEvent (src/sessions/store.ts)\n\nReplace getEventCount (reads entire file, counts lines) with getLastSeq:\n- Read last ~4KB of events.jsonl (fs.read with position = fileSize - 4096)\n- Find last complete JSON line (last newline boundary)\n- Parse it, extract seq field, return seq + 1\n- Empty/missing file returns 0\n- This is O(1) regardless of file size\n\n## Fix 2: Backpressure in session update logger (src/cli/commands/ralph.ts)\n\nReplace fire-and-forget Promise.resolve().then() pattern in createSessionUpdateLogger with a sequential queue:\n- Maintain a queue of pending updates and a processing flag\n- When an update arrives: push to queue, start processing if not already\n- Process loop: shift from queue, await appendEvent, repeat until queue empty\n- This ensures at most ONE appendEvent is in flight at a time\n- Updates are still non-blocking from the caller's perspective (event handler returns immediately)\n- Queue should be bounded (e.g., 1000 entries) — drop oldest if exceeded with a warning\n\n## Files\n- src/sessions/store.ts — getEventCount → getLastSeq\n- src/cli/commands/ralph.ts — createSessionUpdateLogger backpressure queue\n- tests/sessions-store.test.ts — update seq assignment tests\n- tests/ralph.test.ts — update/add logger backpressure tests",

--- Spec Context ---
Implementing: Ralph command - automated task loop

Automated task loop using ACP protocol. Runs claude-agent-acp agent in a loop to process kspec tasks autonomously with full event logging and streaming output.

Acceptance Criteria (27):
  [ac-1]
    Given: ready tasks exist
    When: kspec ralph is run with --max-loops N
    Then: spawns ACP agent and runs up to N iterations
  [ac-2]
    Given: no ready tasks exist
    When: kspec ralph is run
    Then: command exits with message indicating no ready tasks
  [ac-3]
    Given: a loop iteration starts
    When: agent picks and works on a task
    Then: agent uses task start, task note, and task complete commands per working procedure
  [ac-4]
    Given: a loop iteration ends with work still in progress
    When: agent cannot complete the task in one iteration
    Then: agent commits WIP, adds note documenting progress, and task remains in_progress for next iteration
  [ac-5]
    Given: a loop iteration completes (task done or WIP)
    When: there are uncommitted changes
    Then: agent commits the changes with appropriate message
  [ac-6]
    Given: --dry-run flag is provided
    When: kspec ralph --dry-run is run
    Then: shows the prompt that would be sent without executing agent
```

content.oldText:
# Task Work

Structured workflow for working on tasks. Full lifecycle from start through PR merge.

## When to Use

- Starting work on a ready task
- Continuing in-progress or needs_work tasks
- Ensuring consistent task lifecycle with notes and audit trail

**Not for:** Spec creation (use `{skill:writing-specs}`), plan translation (use `{skill:plan}`), or triage (use `{skill:triage}`).

## Inherit Existing Work First

Before starting new work, check for existing work:

```bash
kspec session start  # Shows active work at the top
```

Priority order:
1. **needs_work** — Fix cycle: address review feedback (highest priority)
2. **in_progress** — Continue work already started
3. **ready (pending)** — New work to start

Always inherit existing work unless explicitly told otherwise. This prevents orphaned tasks.

## Task Lifecycle

```
pending → in_progress → pending_review → completed
              ↓              ↓
          blocked        needs_work
                     (→ in_progress → pending_review)
```

| Command | Transition | When |
|---------|-----------|------|
| `kspec task start @ref` | → in_progress | Beginning work |
| `kspec task submit @ref` | → pending_review | Code done, PR created |
| `kspec task complete @ref --reason "..."` | → completed | PR merged |
| `kspec task block @ref --reason "..."` | → blocked | External blocker |

## CLI Lookups

Use CLI commands to find information. **Do NOT search `.kspec/` YAML files manually** — it wastes time and misses context that CLI commands provide (like inherited trait ACs).

| Need | Command |
|------|---------|
| Task details | `kspec task get @ref` |
| Spec + all ACs (own + inherited) | `kspec item get @ref` |
| Trait definition + ACs | `kspec item get @trait-slug` |
| Search by keyword | `kspec search "keyword"` |
| List by type | `kspec item list --type feature` |
| All traits | `kspec trait list` |
| Task's linked spec | `kspec task get @ref` → read `spec_ref` field |

**Key pattern:** When `kspec item get` output shows "Inherited from @trait-slug", run `kspec item get @trait-slug` to see the trait's ACs. One command — do not grep YAML files.

## Workflow Steps

### 1. Choose Task

```bash
kspec tasks ready                # All ready tasks
kspec tasks ready --eligible     # Automation-eligible only (loop mode)
```

### 2. Verify Work Is Needed

Before starting, check if work is already done:

```bash
# Check git history
git log --oneline --grep="feature-name"
git log --oneline -- path/to/relevant/files

# Check existing implementation
kspec item get @spec-ref  # View spec and ACs
```

If already implemented: verify tests pass, AC coverage exists, then `kspec task complete @ref --reason "Already implemented"`.

**Notes are context, not proof.** If a task has notes saying "already done" — verify independently. Run tests, check code, validate against ACs. If a task is in the ready queue, there's a reason.

### 3. Start Task

```bash
kspec task start @ref
```

### 4. Work and Note

Read all ACs (own + trait) before implementing:

```bash
kspec item get @spec-ref  # Shows own ACs AND inherited trait ACs
```

Add notes during work, not just at the end:

```bash
# Good: explains decisions and context
kspec task note @ref "Using retry with exponential backoff. Chose 3 max retries based on API rate limits."

# Bad: no context
kspec task note @ref "Done"
```

Note when you:
- Discover something unexpected
- Make a design decision
- Encounter a blocker
- Complete a significant piece

For tasks that are missing standalone context (for example, generic derived notes), add one structured note before deep implementation work:

```bash
kspec task note @ref "Execution context:
- Background: why this task matters
- Scope: what is in/out for this task
- Files: exact files expected to change
- Verification: tests/commands that prove completion"
```

### 5. Commit

Include task and spec trailers:

```
feat: add user authentication

Implemented JWT-based auth with refresh tokens.

Task: @task-add-auth
Spec: @auth-feature
```

Trailers enable `kspec log @ref` to find related commits.

### 6. Local Review

Run quality checks before submitting. Verify:

- **Own AC coverage** — Each spec AC has a test annotated `// AC: @spec-ref ac-N`
- **Trait AC coverage** — Each inherited trait AC has a test annotated `// AC: @trait-slug ac-N`
- **Tests pass** — Full test suite, not just new tests
- **Code quality** — Matches existing patterns, no duplicated utilities
- **No regressions** — Existing tests still pass

```bash
kspec validate  # Reports uncovered trait ACs as warnings
```

### 7. Submit Task

```bash
kspec task submit @ref
```

Moves task to `pending_review`. Create PR after submitting.

### 8. Complete Task

After PR is merged:

```bash
kspec task complete @ref --reason "Merged in PR #N. Summary of what was done."
```

## Fix Cycle

When inheriting a `needs_work` task:

1. **Find the PR** — Check for review comments
   ```bash
   gh pr list --search "Task: @task-ref" --json number,url
   gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/comments --jq '.[] | {path, line, body}'
   ```

2. **Fix findings** — Address MUST-FIX and SHOULD-FIX items

3. **Push fixes** — Commit with descriptive message
   ```bash
   git add <files> && git commit -m "fix: address review feedback

   Task: @task-slug"
   git push
   ```

4. **Re-submit** — `kspec task submit @ref` (back to pending_review)

You do NOT merge in a fix cycle. The reviewer handles merge decisions.

## Scope Management

### What's In Scope

Tasks describe expected outcomes, not rigid boundaries:

- **Tests need implementation?** Implementing missing functionality is in scope — the goal is verified behavior
- **Implementation needs tests?** Proving it works is always in scope

### When to Expand vs Escalate

**Expand** (do it yourself):
- Additional work is clearly implied by the goal
- Proportional to the original task
- You have the context

**Escalate** (capture separately):
- Scope expansion is major
- Uncertain about the right approach
- Outside your task's domain

**When you notice something outside your task:** Capture it separately (`kspec inbox add` or `kspec task note`). Don't fix it inline — even small detours compound into drift.

## AC Test Annotations

Link tests to acceptance criteria:

```javascript
// AC: @spec-item ac-N
it('should validate input', () => { ... });
```

```python
# AC: @spec-item ac-N
def test_validates_input():
    ...
```

Every AC should have at least one test with this annotation.

## Implementation Quality

Before submitting:

- **Search for existing utilities** — Don't duplicate helpers that already exist
- **Match neighboring file style** — Naming conventions, error handling, imports
- **Run full test suite** — Not just your new tests
- **Validate** — `kspec validate` for spec alignment

## Loop Mode

Autonomous task execution without human confirmation.

```bash
kspec tasks ready --eligible  # Only automation-eligible tasks

- Continuing in-progress or needs_work tasks
- Ensuring consistent task lifecycle with notes and audit trail

**Not for:** Spec creation (use `{skill:writing-specs}`), plan translation (use `{skill:plan}`), or triage (use `{skill:triage}`).

## Inherit Existing Work First

Before starting new work, check for existing work:

```bash
kspec session start  # Shows active work at the top
```

Priority order:
1. **needs_work** — Fix cycle: address review feedback (highest priority)
2. **in_progress** — Continue work already started
3. **ready (pending)** — New work to start

Always inherit existing work unless explicitly told otherwise. This prevents orphaned tasks.

## Task Lifecycle

```
pending → in_progress → pending_review → completed
              ↓              ↓
          blocked        needs_work
                     (→ in_progress → pending_review)
```

| Command | Transition | When |
|---------|-----------|------|
| `kspec task start @ref` | → in_progress | Beginning work |
| `kspec task submit @ref` | → pending_review | Code done, PR created |
| `kspec task complete @ref --reason "..."` | → completed | PR merged |
| `kspec task block @ref --reason "..."` | → blocked | External blocker |

## CLI Lookups

Use CLI commands to find information. **Do NOT search `.kspec/` YAML files manually** — it wastes time and misses context that CLI commands provide (like inherited trait ACs).

| Need | Command |
|------|---------|
| Task details | `kspec task get @ref` |
| Spec + all ACs (own + inherited) | `kspec item get @ref` |
| Trait definition + ACs | `kspec item get @trait-slug` |
| Search by keyword | `kspec search "keyword"` |
| List by type | `kspec item list --type feature` |
| All traits | `kspec trait list` |
| Task's linked spec | `kspec task get @ref` → read `spec_ref` field |
| Task's linked plan | `kspec task get @ref` → if `plan_ref` is non-null, run `kspec plan get @plan-ref` |

**Key pattern:** When `kspec item get` output shows "Inherited from @trait-slug", run `kspec item get @trait-slug` to see the trait's ACs. One command — do not grep YAML files.

## Workflow Steps

### 1. Choose Task

```bash
kspec tasks ready                # All ready tasks
kspec tasks ready --eligible     # Automation-eligible only (loop mode)
```

### 2. Verify Work Is Needed

Before starting, check if work is already done:

```bash
# Check git history
git log --oneline --grep="feature-name"
git log --oneline -- path/to/relevant/files

# Check existing implementation
kspec item get @spec-ref  # View spec and ACs
```

If already implemented: verify tests pass, AC coverage exists, then `kspec task complete @ref --reason "Already implemented"`.

**Notes are context, not proof.** If a task has notes saying "already done" — verify independently. Run tests, check code, validate against ACs. If a task is in the ready queue, there's a reason.

### 3. Start Task

```bash
# Check task links first
kspec task get @ref

# If plan_ref is non-null, load implementation context from the plan
kspec plan get @plan-ref

# Then start work
kspec task start @ref
```

### 4. Work and Note

Read all ACs (own + trait) before implementing:

```bash
kspec item get @spec-ref  # Shows own ACs AND inherited trait ACs
```

Add notes during work, not just at the end:

```bash
# Good: explains decisions and context
kspec task note @ref "Using retry with exponential backoff. Chose 3 max retries based on API rate limits."

# Bad: no context
kspec task note @ref "Done"
```

Note when you:
- Discover something unexpected
- Make a design decision
- Encounter a blocker
- Complete a significant piece

For tasks that are missing standalone context (for example, generic derived notes), add one structured note before deep implementation work:

```bash
kspec task note @ref "Execution context:
- Background: why this task matters
- Scope: what is in/out for this task
- Files: exact files expected to change
- Verification: tests/commands that prove completion"
```

### 5. Commit

Include task and spec trailers:

```
feat: add user authentication

Implemented JWT-based auth with refresh tokens.

Task: @task-add-auth
Spec: @auth-feature
```

Trailers enable `kspec log @ref` to find related commits.

### 6. Local Review

Run quality checks before submitting. Verify:

- **Own AC coverage** — Each spec AC has a test annotated `// AC: @spec-ref ac-N`
- **Trait AC coverage** — Each inherited trait AC has a test annotated `// AC: @trait-slug ac-N`
- **Tests pass** — Full test suite, not just new tests
- **Code quality** — Matches existing patterns, no duplicated utilities
- **No regressions** — Existing tests still pass

```bash
kspec validate  # Reports uncovered trait ACs as warnings
```

### 7. Submit Task

```bash
kspec task submit @ref
```

Moves task to `pending_review`. Create PR after submitting.

### 8. Complete Task

After PR is merged:

```bash
kspec task complete @ref --reason "Merged in PR #N. Summary of what was done."
```

## Fix Cycle

When inheriting a `needs_work` task:

1. **Find the PR** — Check for review comments
   ```bash
   gh pr list --search "Task: @task-ref" --json number,url
   gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/comments --jq '.[] | {path, line, body}'
   ```

2. **Fix findings** — Address MUST-FIX and SHOULD-FIX items

3. **Push fixes** — Commit with descriptive message
   ```bash
   git add <files> && git commit -m "fix: address review feedback

   Task: @task-slug"
   git push
   ```

4. **Re-submit** — `kspec task submit @ref` (back to pending_review)

Tasks describe expected outcomes, not rigid boundaries:

- **Tests need implementation?** Implementing missing functionality is in scope — the goal is verified behavior
- **Implementation needs tests?** Proving it works is always in scope

- Additional work is clearly implied by the goal

- You have the context

**Escalate** (capture separately):
- Scope expansion is major
- Uncertain about the right approach

    ...

```bash
kspec session start  # Shows active work at the top
```

Priority order:
1. **needs_work** — Fix cycle: address review feedback (highest priority)
2. **in_progress** — Continue work already started
3. **ready (pending)** — New work to start

Always inherit existing work unless explicitly told otherwise. This prevents orphaned tasks.

## Task Lifecycle

```
pending → in_progress → pending_review → completed
              ↓              ↓
          blocked        needs_work
                     (→ in_progress → pending_review)
```

| Command | Transition | When |
|---------|-----------|------|
| `kspec task start @ref` | → in_progress | Beginning work |
| `kspec task submit @ref` | → pending_review | Code done, PR created |
| `kspec task complete @ref --reason "..."` | → completed | PR merged |
| `kspec task block @ref --reason "..."` | → blocked | External blocker |

## CLI Lookups

Use CLI commands to find information. **Do NOT search `.kspec/` YAML files manually** — it wastes time and misses context that CLI commands provide (like inherited trait ACs).

| Need | Command |
|------|---------|
| Task details | `kspec task get @ref` |
| Spec + all ACs (own + inherited) | `kspec item get @ref` |
| Trait definition + ACs | `kspec item get @trait-slug` |
| Search by keyword | `kspec search "keyword"` |
| List by type | `kspec item list --type feature` |
| All traits | `kspec trait list` |
| Task's linked spec | `kspec task get @ref` → read `spec_ref` field |

**Key pattern:** When `kspec item get` output shows "Inherited from @trait-slug", run `kspec item get @trait-slug` to see the trait's ACs. One command — do not grep YAML files.

## Workflow Steps

### 1. Choose Task

```bash
kspec tasks ready                # All ready tasks
kspec tasks ready --eligible     # Automation-eligible only (loop mode)
```

### 2. Verify Work Is Needed

Before starting, check if work is already done:

```bash
# Check git history
git log --oneline --grep="feature-name"
git log --oneline -- path/to/relevant/files

# Check existing implementation
kspec item get @spec-ref  # View spec and ACs
```

If already implemented: verify tests pass, AC coverage exists, then `kspec task complete @ref --reason "Already implemented"`.

**Notes are context, not proof.** If a task has notes saying "already done" — verify independently. Run tests, check code, validate against ACs. If a task is in the ready queue, there's a reason.

### 3. Start Task

```bash
kspec task start @ref
```

### 4. Work and Note

Read all ACs (own + trait) before implementing:

```bash
kspec item get @spec-ref  # Shows own ACs AND inherited trait ACs
```

Add notes during work, not just at the end:

```bash
# Good: explains decisions and context
kspec task note @ref "Using retry with exponential backoff. Chose 3 max retries based on API rate limits."

# Bad: no context
kspec task note @ref "Done"
```

Note when you:
- Discover something unexpected
- Make a design decision
- Encounter a blocker
- Complete a significant piece

For tasks that are missing standalone context (for example, generic derived notes), add one structured note before deep implementation work:

```bash
kspec task note @ref "Execution context:
- Background: why this task matters
- Scope: what is in/out for this task
- Files: exact files expected to change
- Verification: tests/commands that prove completion"
```

### 5. Commit

Include task and spec trailers:

```
feat: add user authentication

Implemented JWT-based auth with refresh tokens.

Task: @task-add-auth
Spec: @auth-feature
```

Trailers enable `kspec log @ref` to find related commits.

### 6. Local Review

Run quality checks before submitting. Verify:

- **Own AC coverage** — Each spec AC has a test annotated `// AC: @spec-ref ac-N`
- **Trait AC coverage** — Each inherited trait AC has a test annotated `// AC: @trait-slug ac-N`
- **Tests pass** — Full test suite, not just new tests
- **Code quality** — Matches existing patterns, no duplicated utilities
- **No regressions** — Existing tests still pass

```bash
kspec validate  # Reports uncovered trait ACs as warnings
```

### 7. Submit Task

```bash
kspec task submit @ref
```

Moves task to `pending_review`. Create PR after submitting.

### 8. Complete Task

After PR is merged:

```bash
kspec task complete @ref --reason "Merged in PR #N. Summary of what was done."
```

## Fix Cycle

When inheriting a `needs_work` task:

1. **Find the PR** — Check for review comments
   ```bash
   gh pr list --search "Task: @task-ref" --json number,url
   gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/comments --jq '.[] | {path, line, body}'
   ```

2. **Fix findings** — Address MUST-FIX and SHOULD-FIX items

3. **Push fixes** — Commit with descriptive message
   ```bash
   git add <files> && git commit -m "fix: address review feedback

   Task: @task-slug"
   git push
   ```

4. **Re-submit** — `kspec task submit @ref` (back to pending_review)

You do NOT merge in a fix cycle. The reviewer handles merge decisions.

Tasks describe expected outcomes, not rigid boundaries:

- **Tests need implementation?** Implementing missing functionality is in scope — the goal is verified behavior
- **Implementation needs tests?** Proving it works is always in scope

- You have the context

        "content": "ENRICHMENT — Standalone context for this task:\n\n**What**: When two ULIDs share a prefix (e.g., 01KJ4SNE9... and 01KJ4SNEC...), the default 8-character short ref `@01KJ4SNE` is ambiguous and fails to resolve. ```sh
OK Started task: 01KJDQ1E

--- Spec Context ---
Implementing: Triage CLI Commands

CLI commands for recording, listing, acting on, overriding, and
exporting triage decisions. Follows inbox.ts command registration pattern.


Acceptance Criteria (17):
  [ac-1]
    Given: user runs kspec triage record <inbox-ref> --action promote --reasoning "clear feature request"

    When: the inbox item exists

    Then: creates a TriageRecord with item_snapshot from inbox item,
status triaged, the given action and reasoning, and commits
to shadow branch

  [ac-2]
    Given: user runs kspec triage list

    When: triage records exist

    Then: displays records with ULID prefix, item snapshot (truncated),
status, action, decided_by, and relative time

  [ac-3]
    Given: user runs kspec triage list --status pending

    When: records with various statuses exist

    Then: only records matching the status filter are shown

  [ac-4]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref>

    When: the record has status triaged and action promote

    Then: executes the promote action (creates task from snapshot),
transitions record to acted_on with acted_at and result_ref

  [ac-5]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref> on a record with action delete

    When: the referenced inbox item still exists

    Then: deletes the inbox item without additional confirmation (the
triage decision serves as prior authorization) and transitions
record to acted_on

  [ac-6]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref> on a record with action defer

    When: the record is triaged

    Then: transitions to acted_on with no side effect beyond recording the deferral

  [ac-7]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref> on a record with action spec-gap

    When: the record is triaged

    Then: creates an observation tagged spec-gap with the item snapshot
and reasoning, transitions record to acted_on with result_ref

  [ac-8]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref> on a record with action duplicate

    When: the record is triaged

    Then: deletes the inbox item (prior authorization) and transitions
record to acted_on

  [ac-9]
    Given: user runs kspec triage start

    When: untriaged inbox items exist

    Then: enters interactive mode presenting items one at a time,
prompting for action and reasoning, creating triage records
for each, skipping already-triaged items

  [ac-10]
    Given: the user aborts interactive triage mode with Ctrl+C

    When: some items have been triaged

    Then: all previously committed triage records are preserved

  [ac-11]
    Given: user runs kspec triage record <ref> with --json flag

    When: the command succeeds

    Then: outputs the created triage record as structured JSON

  [ac-12]
    Given: user runs kspec triage override <triage-ref> --action defer --reasoning "not ready yet"

    When: the triage record exists with an existing decision

    Then: updates the record with override_reasoning, override_by,
override_at, and the new action

  [ac-13]
    Given: user runs kspec triage export --format context

    When: triage records exist

    Then: outputs a markdown context block per record with item text,
action, reasoning, decided_by, evidence refs, and outcome

  [ac-14]
    Given: user runs kspec triage export --format json

    When: triage records exist

    Then: outputs a JSON array with full TriageRecord objects

  [ac-15]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref>

    When: the record has status acted_on (already executed)

    Then: returns an error with guidance that the record has already been acted on

  [ac-16]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref>

    When: the record has status pending (no decision yet)

    Then: returns an error with guidance to record a decision first

  [ac-17]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref> with --dry-run flag

    When: the record has status triaged

    Then: shows what action would be taken without executing it


Remember: Add test coverage for each AC and mark tests with // AC: @spec-ref ac-N
```

OK Started task: 01KJDQ1E

--- Spec Context ---
Implementing: Triage CLI Commands

CLI commands for recording, listing, acting on, overriding, and
exporting triage decisions. Follows inbox.ts command registration pattern.


Acceptance Criteria (17):
  [ac-1]
    Given: user runs kspec triage record <inbox-ref> --action promote --reasoning "clear feature request"

    When: the inbox item exists

    Then: creates a TriageRecord with item_snapshot from inbox item,
status triaged, the given action and reasoning, and commits
to shadow branch

  [ac-2]
    Given: user runs kspec triage list

    When: triage records exist

    Then: displays records with ULID prefix, item snapshot (truncated),
status, action, decided_by, and relative time

  [ac-3]
    Given: user runs kspec triage list --status pending

    When: records with various statuses exist

    Then: only records matching the status filter are shown

  [ac-4]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref>

    When: the record has status triaged and action promote

    Then: executes the promote action (creates task from snapshot),
transitions record to acted_on with acted_at and result_ref

  [ac-5]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref> on a record with action delete

    When: the referenced inbox item still exists

    Then: deletes the inbox item without additional confirmation (the
triage decision serves as prior authorization) and transitions
record to acted_on

  [ac-6]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref> on a record with action defer

    When: the record is triaged

    Then: transitions to acted_on with no side effect beyond recording the deferral

  [ac-7]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref> on a record with action spec-gap

    When: the record is triaged

    Then: creates an observation tagged spec-gap with the item snapshot
and reasoning, transitions record to acted_on with result_ref

  [ac-8]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref> on a record with action duplicate

    When: the record is triaged

    Then: deletes the inbox item (prior authorization) and transitions
record to acted_on

  [ac-9]
    Given: user runs kspec triage start

    When: untriaged inbox items exist

    Then: enters interactive mode presenting items one at a time,
prompting for action and reasoning, creating triage records
for each, skipping already-triaged items

  [ac-10]
    Given: the user aborts interactive triage mode with Ctrl+C

    When: some items have been triaged

    Then: all previously committed triage records are preserved

  [ac-11]
    Given: user runs kspec triage record <ref> with --json flag

    When: the command succeeds

    Then: outputs the created triage record as structured JSON

  [ac-12]
    Given: user runs kspec triage override <triage-ref> --action defer --reasoning "not ready yet"

    When: the triage record exists with an existing decision

    Then: updates the record with override_reasoning, override_by,
override_at, and the new action

  [ac-13]
    Given: user runs kspec triage export --format context

    When: triage records exist

    Then: outputs a markdown context block per record with item text,
action, reasoning, decided_by, evidence refs, and outcome

  [ac-14]
    Given: user runs kspec triage export --format json

    When: triage records exist

    Then: outputs a JSON array with full TriageRecord objects

  [ac-15]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref>

    When: the record has status acted_on (already executed)

    Then: returns an error with guidance that the record has already been acted on

  [ac-16]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref>

    When: the record has status pending (no decision yet)

    Then: returns an error with guidance to record a decision first

  [ac-17]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref> with --dry-run flag

    When: the record has status triaged

    Then: shows what action would be taken without executing it


Remember: Add test coverage for each AC and mark tests with // AC: @spec-ref ac-N
```

# Kynetic Spec - Agent Guide

@kspec-agents.md

## Required Include

For Codex and any harness that does not auto-resolve `@file` references: **you MUST read `kspec-agents.md` explicitly before doing any project work**.  
Treat `AGENTS.md` + `kspec-agents.md` as a single instruction set.

## What This Project Is

Kynetic Spec (`kspec`) is a **self-hosting specification and task management system**. The spec files in `.kspec/` define what kspec should do. The TypeScript code in `src/` implements it. They reference each other.

**Key insight**: The spec IS the source of truth for what to build, and the task system tracks progress on building it. When working on this project, you ARE using kspec to build kspec.

## Project Structure

```
kynetic-spec/
├── .kspec/                    # Spec/task state (shadow branch worktree)
│   ├── kynetic.yaml          # Root manifest
│   ├── project.tasks.yaml    # Active project tasks
│   ├── project.inbox.yaml    # Inbox items
│   └── modules/              # Spec items by domain
├── src/                       # TypeScript implementation
│   ├── schema/               # Zod schemas
│   ├── parser/               # YAML loading
│   └── cli/                  # Command handlers
├── templates/agents-sections/ # Static sections for kspec-agents.md
├── packages/web-ui/           # SvelteKit web interface
└── tests/                     # Vitest tests
```

## Agent Instructions Generation

`kspec agents generate` produces `kspec-agents.md` by combining two types of content:

| Source | What it provides | How to change |
|--------|-----------------|---------------|
| **Dynamic data** (from `.kspec/`) | Conventions, workflows, skills | `kspec meta set`, `kspec meta add` |
| **Static templates** (`templates/agents-sections/`) | Quick start, shadow branch, task lifecycle, PR workflow, commit convention, ralph loop, batch usage | Edit the markdown files directly |

Templates ship with the npm package and provide the structural documentation that doesn't change per-project. Dynamic data is project-specific and lives in the shadow branch.

**When to edit templates vs meta:**
- New convention rule → `kspec meta set <domain> --add-rule "..."`
- New workflow → `kspec meta add workflow`
- Changing how a workflow section is *explained* → edit the template file
- Adding a new documentation section → create `NN-section-name.md` (numeric prefix controls order)

## Skill Source of Truth

Do not edit rendered skill files directly in `.agents/skills/`.

- **Core skills** (the ones rendered with `kspec-` prefix under `.agents/skills/`) are authored in `templates/skills/` and listed in `templates/skills/manifest.yaml`.
- **Project/local skills** are stored in `.kspec/skills/` (shadow branch state).
- `.agents/skills/` is rendered output for agent runtimes; regenerate from sources via `kspec skill render` or `kspec setup`.

## Test Helpers

| Helper | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `setupTempFixtures()` | Copy pre-built fixtures to temp dir |
| `createTempDir()` | Create empty temp dir |
| `initGitRepo(dir)` | Initialize git with test config |
| `testUlid(prefix?)` | Generate valid test ULID |
| `testUlids(prefix, count)` | Generate multiple unique ULIDs |
| `kspec(args, cwd)` | Run CLI command, return result |
| `kspecJson<T>(args, cwd)` | Run CLI with --json, return parsed |

See `tests/helpers/cli.ts` for full documentation.

## Daemon Test Architecture

Three approaches, each for different purposes:

1. **Static analysis** (vitest): Read source files, verify patterns. Fast, no runtime.
2. **Unit with isolation** (vitest): Test components in temp dirs with `createTempDir()`.
3. **E2E** (Playwright): Full browser integration. See testing and development conventions.

Multi-project tests use `setupMultiDirFixtures()` for isolated project directories.

## Design Decisions

Key decisions documented in `docs/history/KYNETIC_SPEC_DESIGN.md`:

- **Format**: YAML with Zod validation
- **Schema source**: Zod (TypeScript-native)
- **Architecture**: Library-first, CLI is a consumer
- **Task-spec relationship**: Tasks reference specs, don't duplicate
- **Notes**: Append-only with supersession

--- Spec Context ---
Implementing: Batch Command Execution

Acceptance Criteria (22):
  [ac-stdin]
    Given: JSON array piped via stdin
    When: kspec batch runs with no --file or --commands flag
    Then: Commands are read from stdin and executed in order
  [ac-file]
    Given: --file flag with path to JSON file
    When: kspec batch --file commands.json runs
    Then: Commands are read from the file and executed in order
  [ac-inline]
    Given: --commands flag with JSON string
    When: kspec batch --commands with inline JSON runs
    Then: Inline JSON is parsed and commands execute
  [ac-stop-on-error]
    Given: Default mode (no --continue flag) with 5 commands where command 3 fails at runtime
    When: Batch executes
    Then: In atomic mode: all changes rolled back. In immediate mode: commands 1-2 committed, commands 4-5 not executed. Exit code is 1
  [ac-continue]
    Given: Immediate mode (--continue implies --no-atomic) with 5 commands where command 3 fails at runtime
    When: Batch executes
    Then: All 5 commands are attempted, command 3 failure is recorded, other commands succeed, exit code is 1
  [ac-prevalidate]
    Given: Batch with 3 commands where command 2 has invalid syntax
    When: kspec batch runs
    Then: Validation fails before any execution, no commands run, error identifies the invalid command by index, exit code is 1
  [ac-dry-run]
    Given: --dry-run flag with valid batch
    When: kspec batch --dry-run runs
    Then: All commands are validated but not executed, output shows what would run, no state changes occur
  [ac-forward-ref]
    Given: Batch where command 2 references slug created by command 1
    When: kspec batch runs
    Then: Pre-validation recognizes the forward reference as valid, execution succeeds for both commands
  [ac-single-commit]
    Given: Atomic mode (default) with 3 successful mutating commands
    When: Batch completes successfully
    Then: A single shadow branch commit is created containing all changes (not 3 separate commits)
  [ac-partial-commit]
    Given: Immediate mode with --continue, commands 1-2 succeed, command 3 fails
    When: Batch completes with partial success
    Then: 2 individual commits (commands 1-2), no commit for command 3
  [ac-mutating-only]
    Given: Batch containing a read-only command like item get
    When: kspec batch runs
    Then: Validation rejects with error identifying the non-mutating command
  [ac-confirmation-suppressed]
    Given: Batch containing a command that normally requires confirmation (e.g., item delete without --force)
    When: kspec batch runs
    Then: Command executes without prompting for confirmation (batch mode is implicitly non-interactive)
  [ac-invalid-json]
    Given: Malformed JSON input (from any source)
    When: kspec batch runs
    Then: Parse error with line/position info if available, exit code 1, no commands executed
  [ac-empty-batch]
    Given: Empty JSON array []
    When: kspec batch runs
    Then: Error message says batch contains no commands, exit code 1
  [ac-default-atomic]
    Given: kspec batch runs without --no-atomic
    When: Batch executes
    Then: Atomic mode: commands execute against isolated copy of state
  [ac-atomic-rollback]
    Given: Atomic mode, 5 cmds where cmd 3 fails
    When: Batch encounters failure
    Then: ALL changes discarded, no shadow commit, state identical to before batch, exit 1
  [ac-atomic-isolation]
    Given: Atomic mode, commands modifying state
    When: Batch is executing
    Then: Modifications in isolated copy; other kspec operations see original state
  [ac-no-atomic-flag]
    Given: --no-atomic flag provided
    When: kspec batch runs
    Then: Immediate mode: per-command commits, no rollback
  [ac-immediate-per-commit]
    Given: Immediate mode, 3 successful commands
    When: Batch completes
    Then: 3 individual shadow commits (one per command)
  [ac-immediate-no-rollback]
    Given: Immediate mode, 5 cmds where cmd 3 fails
    When: Batch stops
    Then: Commands 1-2 remain committed, cmds 4-5 not executed, exit 1
  [ac-continue-implies-immediate]
    Given: --continue without --no-atomic
    When: kspec batch runs
    Then: Immediate mode activated implicitly with notice in output
  [ac-json-mode-field]
    Given: --json flag provided
    When: Batch completes
    Then: JSON output includes mode field: atomic or immediate

Remember: Add test coverage for each AC and mark tests with // AC: @spec-ref ac-N
```

# Kynetic Spec - Agent Guide

@kspec-agents.md

## Required Include

For Codex and any harness that does not auto-resolve `@file` references: **you MUST read `kspec-agents.md` explicitly before doing any project work**.  
Treat `AGENTS.md` + `kspec-agents.md` as a single instruction set.

## What This Project Is

Kynetic Spec (`kspec`) is a **self-hosting specification and task management system**. The spec files in `.kspec/` define what kspec should do. The TypeScript code in `src/` implements it. They reference each other.

**Key insight**: The spec IS the source of truth for what to build, and the task system tracks progress on building it. When working on this project, you ARE using kspec to build kspec.

## Project Structure

```
kynetic-spec/
├── .kspec/                    # Spec/task state (shadow branch worktree)
│   ├── kynetic.yaml          # Root manifest
│   ├── project.tasks.yaml    # Active project tasks
│   ├── project.inbox.yaml    # Inbox items
│   └── modules/              # Spec items by domain
├── src/                       # TypeScript implementation
│   ├── schema/               # Zod schemas
│   ├── parser/               # YAML loading
│   └── cli/                  # Command handlers
├── templates/agents-sections/ # Static sections for kspec-agents.md
├── packages/web-ui/           # SvelteKit web interface
└── tests/                     # Vitest tests
```

## Agent Instructions Generation

`kspec agents generate` produces `kspec-agents.md` by combining two types of content:

| Source | What it provides | How to change |
|--------|-----------------|---------------|
| **Dynamic data** (from `.kspec/`) | Conventions, workflows, skills | `kspec meta set`, `kspec meta add` |
| **Static templates** (`templates/agents-sections/`) | Quick start, shadow branch, task lifecycle, PR workflow, commit convention, ralph loop, batch usage | Edit the markdown files directly |

Templates ship with the npm package and provide the structural documentation that doesn't change per-project. Dynamic data is project-specific and lives in the shadow branch.

**When to edit templates vs meta:**
- New convention rule → `kspec meta set <domain> --add-rule "..."`
- New workflow → `kspec meta add workflow`
- Changing how a workflow section is *explained* → edit the template file
- Adding a new documentation section → create `NN-section-name.md` (numeric prefix controls order)

## Skill Source of Truth

Do not edit rendered skill files directly in `.agents/skills/`.

- **Core skills** (the ones rendered with `kspec-` prefix under `.agents/skills/`) are authored in `templates/skills/` and listed in `templates/skills/manifest.yaml`.
- **Project/local skills** are stored in `.kspec/skills/` (shadow branch state).
- `.agents/skills/` is rendered output for agent runtimes; regenerate from sources via `kspec skill render` or `kspec setup`.

## Test Helpers

| Helper | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `setupTempFixtures()` | Copy pre-built fixtures to temp dir |
| `createTempDir()` | Create empty temp dir |
| `initGitRepo(dir)` | Initialize git with test config |
| `testUlid(prefix?)` | Generate valid test ULID |
| `testUlids(prefix, count)` | Generate multiple unique ULIDs |
| `kspec(args, cwd)` | Run CLI command, return result |
| `kspecJson<T>(args, cwd)` | Run CLI with --json, return parsed |

See `tests/helpers/cli.ts` for full documentation.

## Daemon Test Architecture

Three approaches, each for different purposes:

1. **Static analysis** (vitest): Read source files, verify patterns. Fast, no runtime.
2. **Unit with isolation** (vitest): Test components in temp dirs with `createTempDir()`.
3. **E2E** (Playwright): Full browser integration. See testing and development conventions.

Multi-project tests use `setupMultiDirFixtures()` for isolated project directories.

## Design Decisions

Key decisions documented in `docs/history/KYNETIC_SPEC_DESIGN.md`:

- **Format**: YAML with Zod validation
- **Schema source**: Zod (TypeScript-native)
- **Architecture**: Library-first, CLI is a consumer
- **Task-spec relationship**: Tasks reference specs, don't duplicate
- **Notes**: Append-only with supersession

When a trait AC doesn't apply to a specific spec, annotate it as N/A with a reason:

```javascript
// AC: @trait-slug ac-N — N/A: reason why it doesn't apply
```

```python
# AC: @trait-slug ac-N — N/A: reason why it doesn't apply
```

Group N/A annotations together in a dedicated test or at the top of the test file. The `AC:` annotation marker with language-appropriate comment prefix is required — do not use prose comments or bullet lists. The annotation must be machine-parseable.

## Ralph Loop Mode

When running in automated loop mode (ralph):

### The Loop

```
for each iteration:
  1. Ralph checks eligible tasks — if none, exits loop
  2. Agent works on tasks, may create PR(s)
  3. Agent stops responding (turn complete)
  4. Ralph sends reflection prompt
  5. Ralph processes pending_review via subagent
  6. Continue
```

**When you stop responding, ralph continues automatically.** Do NOT call `end-loop` after creating a PR.

### Task Inheritance

Priority: `needs_work` > `in_progress` > `pending`. Always inherit existing work before starting new tasks. (`pending_review` tasks are handled by the review subagent, not the worker.)

### Blocking Rules

**Block only for genuine external blockers:**
- Requires human architectural decision
- Needs spec clarification
- Depends on external API/service not available
- Formally blocked by `depends_on`

**Do NOT block for:**
- Task seems complex (do the work)
- Tests are failing (fix them)
- Service needs running (start it)
- Another task's PR is in CI (not a formal dependency)

**After blocking a task:**
```bash
kspec task block @task --reason "Reason..."
kspec tasks ready --eligible
# If tasks returned: work on next one
# If empty: stop responding — ralph auto-exits
```

**One blocked task is NOT "no more work."** `kspec tasks ready --eligible` output is authoritative.

## Batch Usage

Use `kspec batch` for 2+ sequential write operations — one atomic shadow branch commit instead of N.

### JSON Format

Pipe a JSON array of command objects:

```json
[
  {"command": "task set", "args": {"ref": "@task-slug", "automation": "eligible"}},
  {"command": "task note", "args": {"ref": "@task-slug", "message": "Assessed and marked eligible"}},
  {"command": "inbox add", "args": {"text": "New idea to triage", "tag": ["mvp", "cli"]}}
]
```

Each object has:
- `command` — command path without `kspec` (e.g. `"task add"`, `"item ac add"`)
- `args` — object mapping parameter names to values
- `id` — optional correlation label for error messages

### Argument Rules

| Type | Key format | Example |
|------|-----------|---------|
| Positional (`<ref>`) | Parameter name from signature | `"ref": "@task-slug"` |
| Option (`--spec-ref`) | camelCase or kebab, no `--` | `"specRef": "@spec"` or `"spec-ref": "@spec"` |
| Boolean flag (`--force`) | Flag name, no `--` | `"force": true` |
| Repeatable (`--tag`) | Same key with array value | `"tag": ["cli", "bug"]` |

Boolean `true` emits the flag; `false` omits it. Arrays repeat the flag: `--tag cli --tag bug`.

### Invocation

```bash
echo '[...]' | kspec batch              # stdin (default)
kspec batch --file commands.json        # from file
kspec batch --commands '[...]'          # inline JSON
kspec batch --dry-run                   # validate without executing
kspec batch --continue                  # don't stop on first error
```

### Discovering Commands

```bash
kspec batch commands                    # list all allowed commands
kspec batch commands "task set"         # single command schema
kspec batch commands "task set" --json  # structured output for programmatic use
```

Quote multi-word command paths: `"task set"`, `"item ac add"`, `"meta observe"`.

There are 69 occurrences of `_ulid.slice(0, 8)` across 19 files.

**Where**: All places that format ULID refs for display need to use `shortUlid()` instead of `_ulid.slice(0, 8)`. Key files with hardcoded slicing:

- `src/triage/actions.ts` (1 occurrence) — promote result ref
- `src/parser/validate.ts` (8 occurrences) — validation output
- Several other files with 1-3 occurrences each

The `ReferenceIndex` is already available in most of these contexts (it's built during `initContext()` or `buildIndexes()`).

This suggests either the server is closing connections, the keepalive/heartbeat mechanism is missing, or reconnection resets are happening incorrectly.\n\n**Where**:\n- `packages/web-ui/src/lib/websocket/manager.ts` — The WebSocketManager class. Key areas:\n  - `connect()` (line 150): creates WebSocket, sets up onopen/onmessage/onerror/onclose handlers\n  - `scheduleReconnect()` (line 371): exponential backoff logic, max 10 attempts\n  - `onclose` handler (line 183): triggers reconnect on any close event, even clean ones\n  - No heartbeat/ping mechanism — if the server expects periodic pings, the connection may time out\n- `packages/web-ui/src/lib/stores/connection.svelte.ts` — Connection store wrapping the manager\n- Server-side WebSocket handler (in the daemon code) — check if it sends pings or has idle timeouts\n\n**How**: Investigation and fix areas:\n1. **Add heartbeat/ping**: Implement a periodic ping from client to server (e.g., every 30s). Many WebSocket servers close idle connections after a timeout (often 60s). The client should send a ping command and expect a pong response.\n2. **Don't reconnect on clean close**: The `onclose` handler (line 183) calls `scheduleReconnect()` unconditionally. ```sh
OK Started task: 01KJDQ1G6

--- Spec Context ---
Implementing: Interactive Triage UI

Card-based interactive triage mode in the web dashboard.
One-at-a-time item presentation with action selection,
reasoning input, and real-time updates.


Acceptance Criteria (8):
  [ac-1]
    Given: the user navigates to the triage page

    When: untriaged inbox items exist

    Then: displays a card-based view showing item text, tags, age, and added_by

  [ac-2]
    Given: the user views a triage card for an item with an existing agent triage record

    When: the record has status triaged

    Then: shows the agent recommended action, reasoning, and evidence refs

  [ac-3]
    Given: the user selects an action and enters reasoning

    When: they submit the decision

    Then: creates or updates a triage record via the API and advances to next item

  [ac-4]
    Given: the user disagrees with the agent recommendation
```

```sh
OK Started task: 01KJDQ1G6

--- Spec Context ---
Implementing: Interactive Triage UI

Card-based interactive triage mode in the web dashboard.
One-at-a-time item presentation with action selection,
reasoning input, and real-time updates.


Acceptance Criteria (8):
  [ac-1]
    Given: the user navigates to the triage page

    When: untriaged inbox items exist

    Then: displays a card-based view showing item text, tags, age, and added_by

  [ac-2]
    Given: the user views a triage card for an item with an existing agent triage record

    When: the record has status triaged

    Then: shows the agent recommended action, reasoning, and evidence refs

  [ac-3]
    Given: the user selects an action and enters reasoning

    When: they submit the decision

    Then: creates or updates a triage record via the API and advances to next item

  [ac-4]
    Given: the user disagrees with the agent recommendation

    When: they select a different action with override reasoning

    Then: the triage record captures the override with user attribution

  [ac-5]
    Given: the user is in triage mode

    When: they use next/previous navigation

    Then: they can browse items without committing decisions, and
already-triaged items show their decision state

  [ac-6]
    Given: the triage page is open

    When: another client creates or updates a triage record

    Then: the view updates in real-time via WebSocket triage:updates topic

  [ac-7]
    Given: the user wants to filter items

    When: they use tag or status filters

    Then: the card view shows only matching items with updated progress count

  [ac-8]
    Given: the web UI is in static mode

    When: the user navigates to triage

    Then: triage decisions display read-only with action buttons hidden,
card navigation still works for browsing
```

    AC test coverage analysis: 'kspec coverage @spec-ref' command to scan codebase for '// AC: @spec ac-N' annotations and report which ACs have test coverage vs gaps. Soft check for review, not blocking. Consolidated from @01KFHJNR, @01KFP9A6.

  01KGGG0K (3 weeks ago by @claude) [shadow, dx, cli]
    Shadow sync improvements: (1) Auto-resolve using rebase/merge-driver for cleaner sync, (2) Make sync warnings visible in CLI output (currently silent unless KSPEC_DEBUG=1), (3) Auto-detect common issues with suggested fixes. Consolidated from @01KFTDA7, @01KFHZR4.

  01KGGKNX (3 weeks ago by @claude) [cli, design, dx]
    CLI array field flag patterns: (1) Generic --clear <field> or --<field> [] for clearing arrays, (2) --add-<field> vs multiple flags for append semantics. Design unified approach for depends-on, tags, blocked-by, etc. Consolidated from @01KFGRV6, @01KFR0KN.

  01KGGP9F (3 weeks ago by @claude) [cli, inbox, dx]
    Inbox CLI improvements: (1) Add filtering to list: --before/--after <date>, --author <name> (--tag exists), (2) Add merge command: 'kspec inbox merge @source @target' for consolidating duplicates, (3) Add --priority and --automation flags to promote command. Consolidated from @01KG95JP, @01KG95JQ, @01KG95JS.

  01KGGPJ6 (3 weeks ago by @claude) [workflow, cli, dx]
    Workflow CLI improvements: (1) 'workflow show' should infer active run like 'workflow next', (2) Warn when --input flags passed but step has no inputs defined, (3) Improve 'workflow show' output format with vertical display, status indicators, indented notes. Consolidated from @01KFKSF6, @01KFKSGC, @01KFKTNR.

  01KGGPSR (3 weeks ago by @claude) [cli, validation, ux]
    Spec item slug/addressing improvements: (1) Warn/error on slug collision when creating items, (2) Make nested requirements addressable by slug (currently kspec item ac add @slug fails for items under requirements:). Consolidated from @01KGDCRG, @01KGDCRJ.

  01KGGTT3 (3 weeks ago by @claude) [cli, batch, dx]
    Expand @trait-multi-ref-batch to remaining commands: trait add/remove, task set --automation, inbox delete, task note. Enables batch operations like 'kspec task note @ref1 @ref2 @ref3 "shared content"'. Consolidated from @01KG71J2, @01KG95JM, @01KFVXBM.

  01KGKVK9 (3 weeks ago by @claude) [cli, reflection]
    Add --spec-ref filter to kspec task list command to filter tasks by linked spec item

  01KGQY6Q (3 weeks ago by @claude) [workflow, cli, dx, deferred]
    Workflow lifecycle CLI design (from mining run 01KFS6MJ): kspec workflow complete @run-ref (mark run completed, archive), kspec workflow cancel @run-ref (cancel abandoned run), kspec workflow cleanup --older-than Nd (auto-cancel stale runs). Extends existing @01KFPH39 auto-cleanup with concrete subcommand design.

  01KGVK8R (3 weeks ago by @claude) [cli, dx, reflection]
    Item list --module flag and tree view: kspec item list --module cli to scope output to a specific module. kspec item tree @module for hierarchical view (features -> requirements). Currently 50+ items display flat, making it hard to find the right parent for new specs. Friction: during automation triage had to grep YAML files to find parent specs.

  01KGWG99 (3 weeks ago by @claude) [reflection, sessions, schema]
    Define typed event data schemas per EventType — session.start, session.update (with tool_call/sessionUpdate variants), session.end, prompt.sent, tool.call, tool.result, note. Current z.unknown() data field makes it impossible to reliably query events without reverse-engineering from real JSONL files.

  01KGWQ2T (3 weeks ago by @claude) [deferred]
    Session log compaction: at end of each ralph loop, replace raw events.jsonl with a compiled stats file (event counts by type, tool usage frequency, duration, task transitions, error summary). Keep session folders and context snapshots intact but prune the raw log. This gives trend analysis capability without unbounded log growth. Could be a kspec session compact command or automatic post-loop step.

  01KGWZR7 (3 weeks ago by @claude) [reflection, meta, architecture]
    Active context from meta: use the meta database (observations, conventions, patterns) as a dynamic context source that automatically surfaces relevant entries based on current activity. E.g. when reviewing plan-import code, auto-surface friction observations tagged with plan-import. When doing code review, pull in resolved friction patterns as review priors. Replaces manual markdown maintenance (AGENTS.md, skill docs) with structured data that stays current as observations accumulate. Could use conventions or a new meta item type for durable patterns distinct from one-off observations.

Extract to a shared constant to prevent drift.

Consider: kspec skill, CLI command, or standalone workflow. Re-run after implementing the 6 CLI agent-UX improvements to measure impact.

Currently only comma-separated works. Small fix: change .option('-s, --status <status>') to use Commander's variadic/collect pattern, then feed array into parseMultiStatus().

Could show task state transitions, spec evolution, workflow modifications, etc.

    Version pinning: all projects use whatever global kspec version is installed. No lock file or constraint resolution. Consider adding version constraints to kynetic.yaml manifest.

    Naming inconsistency: isKspecManagedSkill (skill-render.ts) vs isKspecManaged (skill.ts) for same logic. Standardize to one name.

    Redundant platform/tags/depends_on defaults in skill CLI — manually set before SkillSchema.safeParse which already applies them. Remove manual defaults.

  01KHKTNJ5 (1 week ago by @claude)
    deprecated_target warning type reused for skill-specific warnings (depends_on validation, orphaned dirs). Add proper skill warning types for better filtering.

  01KHKVQG (1 week ago by @claude)
    Ralph loop consolidation pass: add a cleanup/consolidation iteration every N PRs or at loop end. The PR-by-PR review process misses cross-PR duplication accumulation — 32 PRs in last loop produced 24 inbox items of tech debt. A periodic consolidation step would catch dead code, duplicated utilities, and superseded implementations before they compound.

  01KHPYJ2 (1 week ago by @claude) [codex, skills]
    Codex skill: handle own-PR reviews — GitHub rejects REQUEST_CHANGES on your own PRs, Codex should use COMMENT event instead. Bundle this fix with skill importing refinement so it propagates to all projects.

  01KHRTEV (1 week ago by @claude)
    Task-specific ephemeral AC: Support acceptance criteria directly on tasks (not just via spec_ref). Useful for implementation requirements, refactoring criteria, and one-off work that doesn't warrant a spec item. Task ACs would be checked during review but wouldn't live in the spec hierarchy. Addresses the gap where plan-imported ACs are behavioral specs vs task-level implementation requirements.

  01KHRX2P (1 week ago by @claude)

  01KHSJJR (1 week ago by @claude)

Currently no easy way to see what happened in a ralph loop iteration without cross-referencing PR timestamps, git log, and task states. A session log showing PR-to-task mapping per loop iteration would help audit and review. Originated from imgen project observation.

Key questions: where does config live, include vs exclude list, defaults, custom sections, ordering, data vs template distinction, migration path. See plan doc for full requirements.

# Kynetic Spec - Agent Guide

@kspec-agents.md

## Required Include

For Codex and any harness that does not auto-resolve `@file` references: **you MUST read `kspec-agents.md` explicitly before doing any project work**.  
Treat `AGENTS.md` + `kspec-agents.md` as a single instruction set.

## What This Project Is

Kynetic Spec (`kspec`) is a **self-hosting specification and task management system**. The spec files in `.kspec/` define what kspec should do. The TypeScript code in `src/` implements it. They reference each other.

**Key insight**: The spec IS the source of truth for what to build, and the task system tracks progress on building it. When working on this project, you ARE using kspec to build kspec.

## Project Structure

```
kynetic-spec/
├── .kspec/                    # Spec/task state (shadow branch worktree)
│   ├── kynetic.yaml          # Root manifest
│   ├── project.tasks.yaml    # Active project tasks
│   ├── project.inbox.yaml    # Inbox items
│   └── modules/              # Spec items by domain
├── src/                       # TypeScript implementation
│   ├── schema/               # Zod schemas
│   ├── parser/               # YAML loading
│   └── cli/                  # Command handlers
├── templates/agents-sections/ # Static sections for kspec-agents.md
├── packages/web-ui/           # SvelteKit web interface
└── tests/                     # Vitest tests
```

## Agent Instructions Generation

`kspec agents generate` produces `kspec-agents.md` by combining two types of content:

| Source | What it provides | How to change |
|--------|-----------------|---------------|
| **Dynamic data** (from `.kspec/`) | Conventions, workflows, skills | `kspec meta set`, `kspec meta add` |
| **Static templates** (`templates/agents-sections/`) | Quick start, shadow branch, task lifecycle, PR workflow, commit convention, ralph loop, batch usage | Edit the markdown files directly |

Templates ship with the npm package and provide the structural documentation that doesn't change per-project. Dynamic data is project-specific and lives in the shadow branch.

**When to edit templates vs meta:**
- New convention rule → `kspec meta set <domain> --add-rule "..."`
- New workflow → `kspec meta add workflow`
- Changing how a workflow section is *explained* → edit the template file
- Adding a new documentation section → create `NN-section-name.md` (numeric prefix controls order)

## Skill Source of Truth

Do not edit rendered skill files directly in `.agents/skills/`.

- **Core skills** (the ones rendered with `kspec-` prefix under `.agents/skills/`) are authored in `templates/skills/` and listed in `templates/skills/manifest.yaml`.
- **Project/local skills** are stored in `.kspec/skills/` (shadow branch state).
- `.agents/skills/` is rendered output for agent runtimes; regenerate from sources via `kspec skill render` or `kspec setup`.

## Test Helpers

| Helper | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `setupTempFixtures()` | Copy pre-built fixtures to temp dir |
| `createTempDir()` | Create empty temp dir |
| `initGitRepo(dir)` | Initialize git with test config |
| `testUlid(prefix?)` | Generate valid test ULID |
| `testUlids(prefix, count)` | Generate multiple unique ULIDs |
| `kspec(args, cwd)` | Run CLI command, return result |
| `kspecJson<T>(args, cwd)` | Run CLI with --json, return parsed |

See `tests/helpers/cli.ts` for full documentation.

## Daemon Test Architecture

Three approaches, each for different purposes:

1. **Static analysis** (vitest): Read source files, verify patterns. Fast, no runtime.
2. **Unit with isolation** (vitest): Test components in temp dirs with `createTempDir()`.
3. **E2E** (Playwright): Full browser integration. See testing and development conventions.

Multi-project tests use `setupMultiDirFixtures()` for isolated project directories.

## Design Decisions

Key decisions documented in `docs/history/KYNETIC_SPEC_DESIGN.md`:

- **Format**: YAML with Zod validation
- **Schema source**: Zod (TypeScript-native)
- **Architecture**: Library-first, CLI is a consumer
- **Task-spec relationship**: Tasks reference specs, don't duplicate
- **Notes**: Append-only with supersession

      "content": "ENRICHMENT — Standalone context for this task:\n\n**What**: The triage page has status and tag filters (lines 326-347 of `packages/web-ui/src/routes/triage/+page.svelte`) but no way to filter triage records by their action type (promote, delete, defer, spec-gap, duplicate). When reviewing triage history, users often want to see \"all promote decisions\" or \"all spec-gap findings\" without scrolling through mixed results.\n\n**Where**: `packages/web-ui/src/routes/triage/+page.svelte`:\n- Existing filters: `filterStatus` (all/untriaged/triaged/acted_on) at line 44, `filterTag` at line 43\n- Filter UI: lines 324-347 (the filter controls div with data-testid=\"triage-filters\")\n- Filtered items computation: `filteredItems` derived at lines 78-96 — currently filters by tag and status only\n- The `TriageAction` type includes: promote, delete, defer, spec-gap, duplicate (defined in `$lib/types/triage`)\n\n**How**:\n1. Add a new `filterAction` state variable: `let filterAction = $state<TriageAction | ''>('')`\n2. Add a new `<select>` element in the filters div (alongside status and tag filters) with options for each action type\n3. Add action filtering to the `filteredItems` derived computation:\n   ```\n   if (filterAction) {\n     items = items.filter((i) => i.record?.action === filterAction);\n   }\n   ```\n4. Include the action filter in the `$effect` that resets `currentIndex` when filters change (line 296-302)\n5. If implementing URL state persistence (task @01KJDQ1F), also sync this filter to URL params\n\n**Done when**:\n- A dropdown/select control for triage action type appears in the filter bar\n- Selecting \"promote\" shows only items with promote decisions\n- Selecting \"spec-gap\" shows only spec-gap items\n- The empty/default option shows all items (no action filter)\n- Changing the filter resets the card navigation index to 0\n- E2E test covers filtering by action type",

      "content": "Implemented triage action-filter support in web UI scope for @interactive-triage-ui ac-7.\n\nChanges in progress:\n- Added action filter state (`filterAction`) and filtering logic in `packages/web-ui/src/routes/triage/+page.svelte` so cards can be filtered by triage decision action.\n- Added action filter `<select>` UI (`data-testid=\"triage-action-filter\"`) using existing ACTION_LABELS.\n- Included action filter in the index-reset effect so changing filters returns card navigation to index 0.\n- Added E2E coverage in `packages/web-ui/tests/e2e/triage.spec.ts` for control visibility and behavior (action filter narrows results and resets card index).\n\nNext: run targeted E2E and validation checks, then full test suite before submit.",
